sections.content: How many people are "officers of non-governmental organisations"?

13,285 people

were counted on the census as "officers of non-governmental organisations" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Officers of non-governmental organisations perform a variety of administrative and clerical tasks in the running of trade associations, employers� associations, learned societies, trade unions, charitable organisations and similar bodies.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "officers of non-governmental organisations" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "officers of non-governmental organisations", 15.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "officers of non-governmental organisations" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "officers of non-governmental organisations" included:

  • road transport drivers (other)
  • roundspersons and van salespersons
  • market and street traders and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "officers of non-governmental organisations" there were more women than men (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

This means "officers of non-governmental organisations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 28.8% and women made up 71.2% of "officers of non-governmental organisations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "officers of non-governmental organisations" included:

  • local government administrative occupations
  • financial administrative occupations (other)
  • waiters and waitresses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "officers of non-governmental organisations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "officers of non-governmental organisations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "officers of non-governmental organisations", 15% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (53.7% compared with 46.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (94.5%) than self-employed (5.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
